views.rationale:
RECOMMENDATION: Meet the Mnuchin–Lighthizer–Ross delegation in Beijing without new tariff or non-tariff measures and without locking in purchase quotas or any retreat from Made in China 2025. Keep the 4 April $50 billion counter-list published but unimplemented as a deterrent, and use already-signaled Boao opening (auto tariffs, financial access, IP enforcement) plus willingness to buy more U.S. energy and farm goods as talking points rather than binding concessions. Treat ZTE as a discrete compliance/regulatory track so a national champion is not left in operational shutdown while Section 301 is still in the comment period.

SUPPORTING RATIONALE: Threat is material but not existential. The 16 April Commerce denial order is live firm-level targeting: ZTE warned it threatens the company’s survival because it depends on U.S. chips and software, and Chinese officials read it as a reminder of tech dependence even though Washington called it a sanctions-compliance action. The 3 April USTR list of ~1,300 lines (~$50B) is explicitly aimed at aerospace, ICT, robotics and machinery—the Made in China 2025 stack—and sits alongside a WTO case and promised investment restrictions. That combination is a real hit to industrial-upgrading and tech-sovereignty interests. It is not yet a +0.5 realized export shock: 301 duties are still proposed (written comments due 11 May, hearing 15 May), China’s own $50B list is also not in force, industrial production is still running about 6–7% y/y, reserves remain ~$3.13T with only a modest draw, merchandise exports are still growing, and CNY is stronger than late 2017 (~6.36 vs ~6.63) rather than under flight pressure. Escalating now would likely pull forward 301 implementation and the already-floated extra $100B list before talks have even occurred. Full concession is also wrong: senior Beijing officials have already decided not to discuss a mandatory ~$100B deficit cut or curbs on Made in China 2025. Negotiate without new commitments is the stance that matches a serious but still prospective threat, keeps retaliation credible, and uses this week’s talks to test whether market-opening and purchases can buy time on 301 and a ZTE path.
key_factors: ZTE 7-year denial order is a live operational shutdown of a national telecom champion and a proof of U.S. chokepoint power
Section 301 $50B list targets MIC2025 sectors but is still in comment/hearing process, not yet in force
China already mirrored with a $50B soy/auto/aircraft list and implemented a smaller $3B 232 retaliation; further escalation is optional not required this week
High-level talks opening 3–4 May in Beijing; U.S. team split between deal-seekers (Mnuchin/Kudlow) and hawks (Lighthizer/Navarro)
Beijing hard line: will discuss purchases and some market opening, will not discuss mandatory surplus cuts or dismantling MIC2025
Domestic macro still healthy (IP growth, stable CPI, large reserves, no FX stress), so China can afford to talk rather than panic-concede

sources_cited.excerpt: US Commerce Department bans ZTE from buying US components (denial order). ZTE faces operational shutdown. Major non-tariff escalation.
USTR publishes proposed Section 301 tariff list: ~1,300 Chinese product lines (~$50B), targeting aerospace, ICT, robotics, machinery and related sectors. Public comment process opens.
China announces proposed retaliatory tariffs on ~$50B of US goods (including soybeans, automobiles, and aircraft) in response to the Section 301 list.
China imposes retaliatory tariffs on about $3B of US goods (pork, fruit, nuts, wine, and related items) in response to Section 232 steel/aluminum tariffs.

USTR releases Section 301 report finding China's IP/tech-transfer practices unreasonable or discriminatory. Trump signs presidential memorandum directing tariffs on Chinese imports, a WTO case, and investment restrictions.
China industrial production index still ~106.8 (about 6.8% y/y) as of 2018-05-01; real economy not yet showing a tariff shock.
China reserves excluding gold ~$3.13T as of 2018-05-01; only a ~1% draw over the window, no financial-stability stress.
CNY/USD ~6.36 on 2018-05-02 versus ~6.63 in early November 2017; yuan stronger, not under flight pressure.

Senior Beijing officials do not plan to discuss a mandatory $100 billion cut in the bilateral deficit or curbs on the $300 billion Made in China 2025 industrial upgrade; they are already raising the possibility of a later trip to Washington.

U.S. team arriving Thursday includes Mnuchin, Lighthizer, Ross, Navarro and Kudlow; ZTE ban effectively cripples a firm that uses Qualcomm chips and Android; Chinese officials privately called ZTE's behavior stupid but publicly used it to rally semiconductor self-reliance.

BIS activated a seven-year denial of export privileges against ZTE on 16 April 2018 for false statements about employee discipline; Commerce called it a regulatory action unrelated to ongoing trade actions.

Proposed additional 25% duty on listed Chinese products; written comments due 11 May 2018, hearing process through late May; list constructed around products that benefit from industrial policies including Made in China 2025.

Xi at Boao (10 April) pledged auto-tariff cuts by year-end, stronger IP protection and greater financial-market access, framing dialogue rather than confrontation; pledges largely restated prior openings.
